character_facts: Tonto and Lothar are in conversation on this page.
Lothar is the one addressed when the claim is made that Steelhead had only one child, a little girl.
Tonto appears to be the more knowledgeable speaker, withholding the full explanation until later.
One of the speakers is highly impatient and threatens violence over unanswered questions.
Steelhead is characterized by one speaker as having acted for love when he saved the girl.
characters_present: an unnamed little girl/daughter of Steelhead (discussed, not seen)
continuity_links: The page explicitly continues an ongoing explanation about the survival of the Metabaron/Castaka line.
The ending banner announces that the answer will continue in the next episode, titled 'Aghora, The Father-Mother...'.
dialogue_meaning: The speakers debate Steelhead's motive for saving a girl; one interprets it as love.
They reject the assumption that Steelhead continued the male line with another woman.
They state that Steelhead's only child was a little girl.
One speaker wants to know how the Castaka/Metabaron lineage continued despite the father-to-son tradition.
The other postpones the explanation because they are compelled to prepare their master's breakfast.
The speakers believe the returning Metabaron does not know where they are, but they still continue their assigned task due to robotic laws or programming.
One speaker reacts with frustration and threatens the other over excessive curiosity.
locations: A ruined or abandoned industrial wasteland
A colossal latticework face-shaped structure in the landscape
lore_facts: The Castaka name is described on this page as traditionally passing from father to son.
According to the speakers, Steelhead's only child was a daughter, not a son.
The speakers refer to 'the laws of robotics' as binding commands they cannot violate.
The speakers serve a master and are responsible for preparing that master's breakfast.
There is an active 'current Metabaron' distinct from Steelhead.
plot_events: Two unseen speakers argue over why Steelhead spared a girl instead of killing all witnesses.
One speaker insists Steelhead saved the girl out of love rather than simple mistake.
The conversation establishes that Steelhead never fathered a son, only a daughter.
A speaker is confused because the Castaka name is said to pass from father to son, and asks how the clan survived.
The explanation is deferred until tomorrow because they must prepare their master's breakfast.
One speaker claims the current Metabaron may soon return and says he does not know their location.
The page ends on a cliffhanger promising the explanation in the next episode.
uncertainties: The speakers themselves are not visually identified; their names come only from the dialogue balloons.
Some dialogue is small and partially hard to read, so wording may be imperfect even though the main points are clear.
It is unclear from this page alone whether the giant face structure is a building, monument, machine, or ruin.
The flying creatures' exact nature is unclear; they appear pterosaur-like or mechanical but are not labeled.
visual_summary: A vast, skeletal metal face or mask rises over a ruined industrial landscape at sunset under a starry sky. Several winged, pterosaur-like flying creatures cross the scene. Most of the page is a conversation in caption balloons, ending with a note that the story continues in the next episode.
